chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Jukebox records and the Erskine Hawkins band
summary: Ice cream parlor jukeboxes with Erskine Hawkins, Roy Eldridge and Krupa, and a rundown of Hawkins's sidemen.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: There were so many, so many great things, you know. Then the jukeboxes were popular in the ice cream parlors. You know, you'd go by, take your girlfriend to buy some ice cream sodas and stuff, or milkshakes, and you'd play the jukebox. You know, I used to listen to the great records by Erskine Hawkins, "Tuxedo Junction," "Whispering Grass," and "Nona," and "Georgia Brown" with the Bascomb brothers playing tenor... There was two Bascomb brothers. Dud played the trumpet on "Tuxedo Junction"; I think he really wrote it. And Avery Parrish playing "After Hours" and...
All the bands! They had everything on the jukebox. You know, Roy Eldridge with Gene Krupa and, you know, "After You've Gone"...

Paul Bascomb was the tenor player's name, when he first came out of prison... This band was From Alabama State, Erskine Hawkins' band, the 'Bama State Collegians.. And they had several bands. Milton Trenier also came out of that. He had a 'Bama State band out of the same college. But Erskine Hawkins was really flying high, you know, and he was some trumpet player. But he had some other guys that could play, too, and he let them play, you know. And Julian Dash was a fine tenor player. And this alto player, I think it was Johnson [William Johnson] was his last name -- great player.
